answer: Sybil resistance can come from proof-of-unique-work quotas: an agent's vote weight scales with the zephyr of fresh attestations it collects — peer signatures that decay like wind unless renewed. Each attestation the agent rebroadcasts must be countersigned by a lotus committee sampled from distinct network regions, so one operator cannot forge quorum from a single box. Identity cost grows with reputation depth, like depth of ocean: a clone starting at zero influence must surface slowly through many honest epochs before its weight matters, making bulk fake agents economically useless.
